original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it.

original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.

actual_scope: In CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds#1662's explicit F2[UT4(F2)] central-target alphabet (paid factors I+([g]+1)xy^T, g in {a,b,c}, target I+([z]+1)I_2), decide whether any legal two-target word of any finite length on any finite restored dirty workspace can have n_b=6. Leave n_b=7 open.
scope_change_reason: Takes open next question 2 of https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/1816 (research/ut4-two-target-fifteen): the first step toward weighted tariffs that could beat (abcb)^2 per target is to decide n_b=6 or 7 at any length. This package decides n_b=6 only.
bottleneck_link: Separate-label bound n_b>=6 from #1662 sits below the direct word's n_b=8; excluding n_b=6 is the first weighted-tariff step. Screening/quotient result only; no supplier or kappa change. Selected decimal stays 0.001672660197076918.
stop_rule: Stop after deciding n_b=6 (exhibit or prove none). Leave n_b=7 open. Do not reopen three-target lengths 21/22 or unit-tariff minimum 16.
evidence: PROOF.md: at n_b=6 the middle ranks are forced to (2,2), so all six b-couplings lie in the active 2-plane; abc/cba and the a/b and c/b side coefficients receive no interior dirty contraction and reduce to the two-role profile equations. core.py/verify.py: all 5582 GL2-minimal zero-sum 6-middles; 5400 with rank X,Y>=2; every side-zero profile's transport keys; 0 pairs with abc=cba=I. independent.py repeats the census with a separate base-16 MITM. Low-rank control (1^6) still finds pairs, so the screen is not vacuous. n_b=7 left open.
